transcript.text: Shark NV602UK has lost loads of suction and whistles. Found a split in the flexible hose near the handle end. Is it the hose I need?

[Heading: Split hose]
Yes, the split hose is almost certainly the cause. A split in the flexible hose creates an air leak which kills suction and often causes a whistling sound as air rushes through the gap. Replacing that specific hose section should restore your suction and silence the noise. Before you buy parts, make sure to also empty the bin and check that the filters are clean and completely dry (washed filters must be left for 24 hours), as these can also reduce suction, but they won't cause a whistle.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Thanks. I already cleaned the filters and emptied the bin last week and it made little difference. Do I need just the hose, or the hose and handle assembly? I'm not sure which part to order for the NV602UK.

[Heading: Split flexible hose]
You will need the flexible hose that includes the handle end. On the Shark NV602UK, this hose is typically sold as a single assembly because it connects directly into the handle and body seals; buying just the loose tube often won't fit or seal correctly. Search for "Shark NV602UK flexible hose" or "Shark NV602UK hose assembly" to ensure you get the correct part with the right connectors. Once fitted, reassemble carefully so all clips are secure to prevent further air leaks.
